title: My Elevation: What Is My Elevation Right Now?
description: Find your current elevation instantly with My Elevation — GPS position plus terrain model, shown in feet and metres with a gauge. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, standing in Denver your elevation reads about 5,280 feet — while the same tap in Death Valley's Badwater Basin reads −282 feet, below the level of the sea itself.
quick_answer: My Elevation tells you the elevation where you are standing right now, combining your device's GPS position with terrain-model data. Press the button and read your height above sea level in feet and metres — for trailheads, road trips, flights of curiosity and settling 'how high are we?' arguments.

examples.label: Example · GPS height versus ground height

body.t: Your phone's raw GPS altitude is measured from a mathematical model of sea level (the geoid's rougher cousin, the ellipsoid) and can sit tens of metres off the terrain figure. This page reads the terrain model at your GPS position, which is why its number matches maps and summit signs better.
Stand on the Dead Sea shore and the gauge goes negative — about −430 m (−1,412 ft), the lowest dry ground on Earth. The minus sign is real geography, not an error.

faq: Why does my watch show a different altitude?

Watches with barometric altimeters measure air pressure and convert it; pressure weather moves their answer by tens of metres over a day. This page's terrain figure is fixed to the ground — boring, and therefore stable.
Indoors or in a city canyon?
GPS position degrades among tall buildings, and elevation follows position. Step into the open for the reading you quote.
On a plane or a train?
The terrain model reads the ground below, not your cabin — at cruise you will see the valley's elevation, not 35,000 ft. Barometric apps own the cabin question.
Both, always — this site shows imperial and metric together so no reader converts in their head.
A single GPS fix for one reading is a sip, not a drain. The page does not track you continuously.
Elevations are orthometric: height above the geoid, the equipotential surface 'mean sea level' is measured from — the same reference as maps and surveys, not the ellipsoid raw GPS uses.
Terrain data is modern; land mostly keeps its height, but reservoirs, mines and suburbs have moved some of it since any given year.
